newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Northern posts modest profits rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Northern posts modest profits rise.

text.p: British food and dairy company Northern Foods Plc on Tuesday posted a modest 2.3 percent increase in its full-year profits to 127 million pounds ($207.7 million) as it issued a warning about the state of the dairy industry.
Chairman Christopher Haskins said he expected large-scale consolidation in the industry as some players were losing money amid serious overcapacity.
"Three dairies have gone bust in the last 12 months. There's the Waterford and Avonmore merger in Ireland and we bought a UHT plant from Scottish Pride," Haskins told Reuters in an interview.
"We think one or two of our competitors are losing money and that can't last," he added.

There remains intense pressure on dairy companies from supermarkets to reduce their milk prices, so even if they are able to agree more favourable terms with farmers, that saving is absorbed by the retailers.
Northern, Unigate and Dairy Crest have also been squeezed by the collapse in world commodity prices in the last year.

Dairy companies produce large quantities of semi-skimmed and skimmed liquid milk of which butter fat is a by-product. Butter fat prices on world commodity markets have fallen sharply over the last year.
Northern reported a 26 percent drop in profits from its dairy division to 44.8 million for 1996/97 due to the 17 million pound impact of lower commodity prices.
If approved, the merger of Ireland's Waterford Foods and Avonmore Foods would create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth-largest milk processor in the world.

"There are dairy mergers going on world-wide, in Australia, New Zealand, Holland and France, it's happening all over the world as there is too much capacity and everyone is getting on with sorting it out," Haskins said.

However, he said, Northern's dairy business was now staging a recovery in profits after a fall in raw liquid milk prices. The comments helped lift the group's share price 3-1/2p to 206p in early trade.
Farmer-owned group Milk Marque, which supplies some 60 percent of milk in England and Wales, reduced its prices to 22.1 pence a litre from about 25 pence from April 1.

Haskins said the company planned to raise its investment programme this year by some 35 million pounds to about 100 million now that the management focus on shutting dairies and re-shaping its doorstep delivery business was complete.

Most of the investment will be directed at prepared foods where Northern has factories producing ready-made foods like pies and sandwiches for Marks and Spencer Plc, worth 300 million pounds in sales a year.
The prepared foods division showed a strong 20 percent rise in trading profits to 98.6 million in the year.
"Food is cheaper now than a year ago and competition among supermarkets is still pretty heavy so our main gains are coming through improved productivity," Haskins said.

Total group sales were 3.3 percent lower in the year ending March 31 at 1.883 billion, with continued growth in prepared foods more than offset by the effects of changes and lower commodity prices on the dairy side.
Meat products turnover was 4.7 percent down at 227.3 million pounds after an estimated 12 million pound hit from the continued scare over the spread of mad cow disease to humans.
